points.text: Chance correction assumes uniform guessing and pre/post independence, unrealistic for LLMs
Chance correction not empirically validated (logit/multi-sample estimates, simulation)
Dataset-level correction cannot identify individually forgotten items, undermining per-sample motivation
F_true is not the conditional rate the introduction claims to measure
Worked example does not match the formulas
Clipping at zero biases small-effect estimates upward
Benchmarks not all pure k-way MCQ; varying k applicability not discussed
Stochastic single-sample decoding creates flips; no same-checkpoint noise control
No confidence intervals, bootstrap or seed variance
'Low/moderate/high' never defined by thresholds
Base few-shot vs post-trained chat prompting confounds pre/post comparison
Format/extraction failures counted as forgetting; no robust answer extraction
Different length caps may truncate long CoT
Public checkpoints with uncontrolled recipes confound stage and size comparisons
Scaling and causal claims rest on few non-matched points without statistics
No controlled data-scale study; 'map at scale' framing overstated
Forgetting measured only on MCQ; generation and other capabilities not covered
Headline conclusion over-reaching; Table 1 compares studies with different protocols
Table 1 Level labels subjective
Merging section thin: few models, two-checkpoint interpolation, no α ablation; conclusion too general
Metric novelty limited relative to existing flip analysis and guessing correction
Inconsistent claims between abstract, captions and results
Typos and duplicate references
Results mostly in figures with numbers only in appendix
Category clustering procedure undescribed; grouping may be post hoc
Explains what causes forgetting/transfer but not why (e.g. culture, reasoning)
Mixed large-scale effects unresolved; data diversity, duration, objective not tested
Merging conclusion based only on two-checkpoint merging; no multi-checkpoint or TIES
MCQ-only evaluation; generative settings not validated
Extensive experimental report with limited conceptual or theoretical insight
Findings described with vague qualitative terms
Training variables (learning rate, data volume) uncontrolled; findings may reflect confounds
Uniform independent guessing assumption idealistic; robustness checks needed
No variance, confidence intervals, significance or multiple-comparison correction for flips
Temperature 0.6 single run; flip stability across seeds not evaluated
Evaluation mostly MCQ; no open generation, code or tool tasks
MCQ focus may not generalize to open-ended tasks
Uniform guessing correction oversimplifies and may distort forgetting
No deep analysis of why stages cause particular effects
